AA Driving School learner, Christchurch Common questions Expand All Should I get professional driving lessons? AA Driving School professional driving lessons are highly recommended as they provide structured training tailored to your experience level, helping you build confidence, develop safer driving habits, and improve your chances of passing your driving test. How many lessons will I need? The number of lessons you need will depend on your driving experience, confidence and learning pace. Some learners need only a few lessons to prepare for a test, while others benefit from more structured coaching. Our 5 Lesson Package offers great value and is a popular choice, giving you enough time to build key skills, gain confidence and receive personalised feedback from your instructor. How do I book a driving lesson? Watch the step by step video for a detailed explanation of how to book AA Driving School lessons. How can I reschedule driving lesson? To reschedule a driving lesson, you will need to cancel your existing lesson first. Once the lesson has been cancelled, the credit will be available in your account, which you can then use to rebook a lesson at your preferred date and time. How can I cancel a driving lesson? You can cancel a lesson by logging in to your AA Driving School profile and clicking the “X” next to the booking you wish to cancel. Once selected, confirm the cancellation to proceed. Can I get a refund for my unused credits? If you have unused credits and would like to request a refund, please contact our team by calling 0800 223 748 or emailing ADriverTraining@aa.co.nz . Refund requests will be reviewed in accordance with our terms and conditions , and our team will advise you of the available options. Book a course A safer driver in 9 hours The AA Defensive Driving Course is an NZTA approved Advanced Driving Course aimed at educating drivers how to be safer on the roads. What does the course include? Four classroom sessions, an online hazard perception component and a one-hour in-car assessment. The following four steps must be completed in order. Four classroom sessions Four two-hour sessions (8 hours in total). Interactive group theory using real driving situations filmed on NZ roads. Covers risks, observation and hazard identification. The four sessions must be completed in order. Need to bring a support person or reader/writer assistance? Contact us before the course date. Online hazard perception Practice hazard identification and visual search online. Account valid for 28 days. Unlimited attempts. Minimum score: 80% - certificate must be shown to the tutor before the in-car assessment. In-car session (1 hour) Individual driving assessment in your own vehicle. The instructor will assess understanding and demonstration of the theory learnt in the classroom sessions. Must be completed within 60 days of your last classroom session. Get your certificate Issued after: Completing coursework. Achieving at least 80% in online hazard perception. Passing the in-car session. If you're eligible to reduce the time on your restricted licence* take your certificate when you apply for your full licence. * Reduction only applies to those eligible to apply for their full licence prior to 25 January 2027; drivers aged 25+ may receive a reduction from six to three months. The AA Defensive Driving Course is an NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi-approved advanced driving course available across New Zealand. It combines interactive learning based on real driving situations on New Zealand roads with online hazard training and an individual in-car assessment. The course is designed to help drivers identify hazards, reduce crash risk, improve safe-driving skills and prepare for the next stage of licensing. Is the AA Defensive Driving Course worth it? The AA Defensive Driving Course can be worthwhile if you want to become a safer, more confident driver, improve hazard awareness or prepare for a practical driving test. It provides structured theory, online practice and a one-hour in-car assessment with practical feedback. Eligible restricted drivers may also be able to apply for their full licence up to six months earlier under the current Graduated Driver Licensing System; check the latest NZTA eligibility rules to confirm. When should I take a defensive driving course? It is generally best to take the AA Defensive Driving Course after you have obtained your restricted licence, because the course helps build a strong foundation as you begin driving more independently. Experienced learner licence holders who are confident drivers can also attend and must be able to complete the in-car assessment in their own vehicle. Full licence holders can take the course to refresh their skills, and it may also suit police recruits or people completing a court referral or Police Diversion programme. What do you learn in a defensive driving course? The AA Defensive Driving Course teaches you to assess and identify hazards, improve visual-search techniques, understand driving risks and road conditions, and apply safer driving practices. The nine-hour course includes four two-hour classroom sessions completed in order, online eDrive learning using real New Zealand road scenarios, and a one-hour individual in-car assessment. The eDrive component requires a score of at least 80%, and the in-car assessment must be successfully completed within 60 days of the final classroom session. How do I book an AA Defensive Driving Course? Book an AA Defensive Driving Course online through the AA Defensive Driving Course page by selecting ‘Book a course’, choosing an available location and course, and paying online. Courses are available at locations across New Zealand. The AA Defensive Driving Course is an NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi-approved advanced driving course available across New Zealand. It combines interactive learning based on real driving situations on New Zealand roads with online hazard training and an individual in-car assessment. The course is designed to help drivers identify hazards, reduce crash risk, improve safe-driving skills and prepare for the next stage of licensing. Is the AA Defensive Driving Course worth it? The AA Defensive Driving Course can be worthwhile if you want to become a safer, more confident driver, improve hazard awareness or prepare for a practical driving test. It provides structured theory, online practice and a one-hour in-car assessment with practical feedback. Eligible restricted drivers may also be able to apply for their full licence up to six months earlier under the current Graduated Driver Licensing System; check the latest NZTA eligibility rules to confirm. Proof of your current New Zealand address. Your glasses or contact lenses if you require them. Completed DL1 application form (or you can complete it at the AA Driver Licensing outlet on the day). A medical certificate if required. Payment for the application or test fee . Yourself! Arrive a few minutes early so you don’t miss your appointment. You must be at least 16 years old before you can book and sit the learner licence theory test, and you’ll need to bring evidence of your identity. Can I book the test online or over the phone? Some AA Driver Licensing outlets allow you to book your test online. For all others, you will need to do this in person. Is there an eyesight test? Yes. If you don't pass your learner licence theory test the first time, your application fee covers a second attempt. You will need to book another time to sit this. For each test after the second attempt, there is an additional fee. What will I get if I pass? If you pass, you'll receive a temporary learner licence to use until your photo licence arrives in the mail. You can also purchase L plates if you need them. Learn what the test involves, the common faults to avoid, and how a practice test with an AA Instructor helps you pass. When you're ready to sit your test, book it at an AA Driver Licencing outlet. Book a practice test Find AA Driver Licensing outlet near me Before you book your test You need to make sure you're eligible and ready. You'll need the right level of driving skill and on-road experience to pass. Be at least 16½ years old. Held your learner licence for at least 6 months. Be confident with the driving skill and on-road experience the test requires. What happens on test day A Driving Testing Officer will carry out the practical driving test. Here's how the test works. Check in Arrive early to the location of your test, and remember to bring your learner licence and L plates. Vehicle check The Testing Officer makes sure your car is safe and roadworthy. This includes having a valid vehicle licence (rego) and Warrant of Fitness. Drive the route You drive a set route while the Officer assesses your skills. The driving test is 45 minutes, with an additional 15 minutes to check the vehicle before the test and provide feedback after. Get your result You find out whether you passed on the day. If you are successful, you'll be issued a temporary licence until your new one is sent to you. Common faults to avoid These are the slip-ups that catch learners out most often. error Failing to look The most common reason for a fail is not checking mirrors and blind spots. Make sure you do this before moving off, turning a corner or changing lanes. error Rolling through stops Failing to come to a complete stop at stop signs, or not giving way correctly at intersections. error Speed not matched to conditions Driving too fast for the road, or so cautiously you hold up traffic, both count against you. error Poor lane position & signalling Drifting in the lane, or signalling too late (or not at all) before a turn or merge. You can find a full list of critical errors and immediate fail errors on the NZTA's website. directions_car_filled Not sure you're ready? No additional fee is required if you change or cancel your test booking. Frequently asked questions Expand All How do I prepare for my restricted driving test? You can prepare for your restricted licence test by taking driving lessons with AA Driving School. Our qualified instructors will help you build safe driving skills, gain confidence on the road, and understand what to expect during the test. Can I take a practice restricted driving test before the real one? Yes. AA Driving School offers a Practice Restricted Licence Test, which is designed to simulate the conditions of the real restricted licence test. During the session, an AA Driving Instructor will assess your driving, identify any areas for improvement, and provide feedback to help you prepare for the actual test. How do I get my restricted licence in New Zealand? To be eligible to sit your restricted licence, you need to be 16 1/2 and have held your learner licence for at least six months. You also need to be confident that you have the driving skill and on-road experience the test requires. AA Driving School lessons can help you with this. Once you're ready, you can book in for your restricted licence test at an AA Driver Licensing outlet. What happens during the restricted licence driving test? Before you start your test, the Testing Officer will make sure your car is safe and roadworthy. This includes having a valid vehicle licence (rego) and Warrant of Fitness. The actual test is around 45 minutes during which the Testing Officer will assess your skills. At the end of the test, you will be given some feedback and told if you have passed. What are the most common reasons people fail the restricted test? Some of the most common reasons people fail their restricted test are: Failing to check mirrors and blind spots Failing to come to a complete stop at stop signs Speed not matching driving conditions, and Poor lane position & signalling Who runs the practical test? The restricted licence practical test is conducted by an NZTA appointed Driving Testing Officer (DTO). On the day of your test, remember to: Bring your current learner licence. Arrive on time. Make sure you're well prepared before sitting the test. You won't be able to drive if you don't have your learner licence with you. What if I don't pass? If you don't pass your restricted licence test, you'll need to book another test before you can try again. To improve your chances of passing, it's recommended that you: Complete at least 120 hours of supervised driving practice (professional lessons count as three hours each).
